reference.text:
[context] There
[context] stood in truth according to the common and received account the feet of our Lord and Saviour, Himself the Word of God, through that tabernacle of humanity He had borne up the Mount of Olives to the cave that is shewn there; there He prayed and delivered to His disciples on the summit of the Mount of Olives the mysteries of His end, and thence He made His Ascension into heaven, as Luke tells us
in the Acts of the Apostles, saying that while the apostles were with Him on the Mount of Olives: "While they beheld he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight. And as they gazed steadfastly into heaven while he went up, behold two men stood by them in white apparel, who also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing into heaven? This same Jesus that is taken up from you into heaven shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven." To which he adds: "Then they returned from the mount called the Mount of Olives, which is opposite to Jerusalem." The Mount of Olives is therefore literally opposite to Jerusalem and to the east of it, but also the Holy Church of God, and the mount upon which it is founded, of which the Saviour teaches: "A city set on a hill cannot be hid," raised up in place of Jerusalem that is fallen never to rise again, and thought worthy of the feet of the Lord, is figuratively not only opposite to Jerusalem, but east of it as well, receiving the rays of the divine light, and become
much before Jerusalem, and near to the Sun of Righteousness Himself, of Whom it is said: "And on them that fear me shall the sun of righteousness arise." And if it says next: "That the Mount of Olives shall be divided, half of it to the east and towards the sea, a very great chasm, and half of it shall lean towards the north, and half of it towards the south," it possibly shews the expansion
of the Church throughout the whole inhabited world, for it has filled the east, and the western and eastern nations; it stretches to the western sea, and the isles therein; yea, it has reached to west and south, and to north and north-east. On all sides and everywhere the Church figuratively called the Olive of the Lord is planted. And it is possible that by its division is figuratively meant the schisms and heresies and moral declensions in everyday life that have taken place in the Church of Christ, and are even now taking place; for it says, the mountain shall be divided, half of it towards the east and the sea, a very great chasm, and half of it shall lean towards the north, and half of it towards the south, as being divided into four parts, two of which are worthier and better, and two the reverse. And note in this passage how the part to the east and the part to the south may refer to two sections of those who have made progress in the things of God, the first those who are perfected in knowledge and reason and the other graces of the Holy Spirit; and the second, those who live a good life but pass their time in ways self-chosen. And the other two parts separated from the first, one to the sea and one towards the north, both signify tendency to evil. For "from the face of the north," he says, "shall be burned the evil of all the inhabitants of the earth," while the Dragon is said to have his home in the sea. So that, probably, two kinds of character in those that fall away from the Church, the morally sinful, and the one who slips away from healthy and orthodox knowledge, are here
figuratively represented by the prophecy as divisions in the Mount of Olives. To this he adds afterwards: "And the valley of my mountains shall be closed up, and the cleft of my mountains shall be joined unto Asael, and shall be closed up as it was blocked up in the days of the earthquake in the days of Ozias king of Judah."

text:
<meta>This page continues Eusebius’s commentary on the prophecy of Zechariah regarding the Mount of Olives. Having established the mountain as a symbol for the Church, he now cites the Book of Acts to link the physical location to the Ascension of Christ and provides a spiritual interpretation of the mountain "splitting" into four directions.</meta>

->### EVANGELICAL PROOF, Book 6###<-

> „ ...the **Acts of the Apostles** teaches this, saying: 'While they were looking on, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him out of their sight. And while they were gazing into heaven as he went, behold, two men stood by them in white robes, who also said, "Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven."' To which he <note>The author of Acts, Luke</note> adds: 'Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem.'</quote> <note>Acts 1:9–12</note>

Indeed, according to the literal word, the Mount of Olives is "opposite Jerusalem," being the mountain that lies to its east. However, according to its deeper meaning <term>dianoia: the spiritual or underlying intent of a text</term>, it is the **Holy Church of Christ**, the mountain upon which she is founded. Concerning this, the Savior teaches:

> „ **"A city set on a hill cannot be hidden."** <note>Matthew 5:14</note>

This Church has been raised up in place of the fallen Jerusalem which did not rise again, and it is "trodden by the feet of the Lord." It is not only "opposite Jerusalem," but also "to the east" of it, having received the first rays of the light of godliness. It has become far superior to the old Jerusalem, drawing near to the **Sun of Righteousness** itself, of whom it has been said:

> „ **"But for you who fear my name, the Sun of Righteousness shall rise."** <note>Malachi 4:2</note>

The text follows by saying that the Mount of Olives shall be split—half of it toward the east and the sea <note>The "sea" refers to the West/Mediterranean</note>, a very great chasm <note>original: "χάος μέγα" (chaos mega); often translated as "valley" in biblical contexts, but Eusebius emphasizes the scale of the division</note>, and half of it shall tilt toward the north and half toward the south. This can signify the expansion of the Church throughout the whole inhabited world. It fills the "east," representing the eastern nations and the dawn. It extends even to the "western sea" and the islands within it. Furthermore, it has reached the "south" and the "meridian," as well as the "north" and the "arctic." For everywhere, the Church—this "valley" of the Lord mentioned in the prophecy—has been victoriously planted.

One can also interpret this "splitting" of the Church of Christ as an allusion to the schisms and **heresies** that have occurred and continue to occur, as well as the falls in morals and lifestyle. For the prophecy says the mountain shall be divided into two, then into four parts: half toward the east, half toward the sea (a very great chasm), half toward the north, and half toward the south. Thus, it is divided into four parts: two of these are more venerable and better, while two are their opposites. 

Consider whether, through these, the "east" and the "south" signify the two ranks of those who have attained progress in God. One rank consists of those perfected in knowledge, reason, and the other gifts of the Divine Spirit; the other consists of those who live uprightly and persevere in blessings. The remaining two parts, separated from the former, would be the "sea" and the "north," both signifying a leaning toward wickedness. For it is said:

> „ **"From the north, evil shall flare up upon all the inhabitants of the land."** <note>Jeremiah 1:14</note>

And it says the "dragon" makes its dwelling in the "sea." <note>Cf. Isaiah 27:1</note> Therefore, it is fitting that here, too, two types of those who fall away from the Church are shown: those who sin in matters of knowledge <note>Heresy</note> and those who sin in their character <note>Immorality</note>. These are the divisions of the symbolic Mount of Olives hinted at by the prophecy. Following these things, it is added:

> „ **"And the valley of my mountains shall be blocked up, and the valley of the mountains shall be joined as far as Azal; and it shall be blocked up as it was blocked up in the face of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, King of [Judah]."** <note>Zechariah 14:5</note>

<summary>Eusebius interprets the splitting of the Mount of Olives in Zechariah's prophecy as a dual metaphor for the Church’s global expansion and the internal divisions caused by heresy and moral failure.</summary>
<keywords>Mount of Olives, Acts of the Apostles, Ascension, Sun of Righteousness, Schism, Heresy, Geography of the Church, Zechariah 14</keywords>

<header>EVANGELICAL DEMONSTRATION Book VI</header>

> "in the Acts of the Apostles he teaches, saying, while they were watching he was lifted up, and a cloud took him from their sight. And as they were gazing into heaven while he was going, behold, two men stood by them in white robes, who also said, Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him going into heaven." To which he adds, saying, "Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem." It is indeed

according to the literal word "near Jerusalem," the mount of Olives, which is indicated as being to the east of it. Nevertheless, according to the spiritual sense, the holy Church of Christ, and the mountain upon which it has been founded, concerning which the Savior teaches, saying, "A city set on a hill cannot be hidden," has been raised up in place of the fallen and unrisen Jerusalem,

and is trodden by the feet of the Lord. It is not only "near" Jerusalem, but also to the east of it, having received the rays of the light of godliness, and having become much earlier than Jerusalem, and drawing near to the Sun of righteousness itself, concerning whom it has been said, "But to you who fear me, the Sun of righteousness shall rise." And what he says next, that "the mount of Olives shall be split, half of it toward the east and the sea, a very great chasm, and half of it shall incline toward the north, and half of it toward the south," can signify the spreading of the Church throughout the whole inhabited world of men, since it has filled the sunrises, and the eastern nations themselves. It extends also to the western sea, and the islands within it. Moreover, it has reached even to the south and the midday, and toward the north, and the arctic regions. For everywhere the entire valley of the Lord, who is foretold as victorious, namely his Church, has been planted. But it is also possible, according to the spiritual sense, to hint at the schisms and heresies that have occurred, and still occur today, within the Church of Christ, as well as the moral lapses and falls in life. For he says the mountain will be split and divided in two, half of it toward the east, half of it toward the sea, a very great chasm, and half of the mountain will incline toward the north, and half of it toward the south. As if to be divided into four parts, two being the more solemn and better, and two the opposites. And see whether, through these, the parts toward the east and toward the south might signify the two orders of those who have attained progress according to God. One order consists of those perfected in knowledge and word, and in the other gifts of the divine Spirit; the other consists of those who succeed through their way of life, and who persevere in blessings. The remaining two parts, divided from the former, would be those toward the sea and toward the north,

> "both signified as being toward wickedness. For from the north, he says, evils will be kindled upon all who dwell on the earth; and he says the dragon makes his dwelling upon the sea; so that reasonably here, too, two ways of those falling away from the Church are indicated, both those who sin in knowledge and those who sin in character, so that these are the divisions of the mount of Olives hinted at by the prophecy." Following these, it is added, "And the valley of my mountains shall be stopped up, and the valley of the mountains shall be joined as far as Asael; and it shall be stopped up just as it was stopped up from the face of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah the king."

<summary>Eusebius interprets the prophecy of the Mount of Olives splitting in Zechariah as a dual allegory: first, the global expansion of the Church in all directions, and second, the division of the Church into different spiritual states and the emergence of heresies.</summary>
<keywords>Mount of Olives, Church, Jerusalem, prophecy, Zechariah, schism, heresy, spiritual interpretation</keywords>

<header>EVANGELICAL DEMONSTRATION Book VI</header>

> "in the Acts of the Apostles he teaches, saying, while they were watching he was lifted up, and a cloud took him from their sight. And as they were gazing into heaven while he was going, behold, two men stood by them in white robes, who also said, Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him going into heaven." To which he adds, saying, "Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem." It is indeed

according to the literal word "near Jerusalem," the mount of Olives, which is indicated as being to the east of it. Nevertheless, according to the spiritual sense, the holy Church of Christ, and the mountain upon which it has been founded, concerning which the Savior teaches, saying, "A city set on a hill cannot be hidden," has been raised up in place of the fallen and unrisen Jerusalem,

and is trodden by the feet of the Lord. It is not only "near" Jerusalem, but also to the east of it, having received the rays of the light of godliness, and having become much earlier than Jerusalem, and drawing near to the Sun of righteousness itself, concerning whom it has been said, "But to you who fear me, the Sun of righteousness shall rise." And what he says next, that "the mount of Olives shall be split, half of it toward the east and the sea, a very great chasm, and half of it shall incline toward the north, and half of it toward the south," can signify the spreading of the Church throughout the whole inhabited world of men, since it has filled the sunrises, and the eastern nations themselves. It extends also to the western sea, and the islands within it. Moreover, it has reached even to the south and the midday, and toward the north, and the arctic regions. For everywhere the entire valley of the Lord, who is foretold as victorious, namely his Church, has been planted. But it is also possible, according to the spiritual sense, to hint at the schisms and heresies that have occurred, and still occur today, within the Church of Christ, as well as the moral lapses and falls in life. For he says the mountain will be split and divided in two, half of it toward the east, half of it toward the sea, a very great chasm, and half of the mountain will incline toward the north, and half of it toward the south. As if to be divided into four parts, two being the more solemn and better, and two the opposites. And see whether, through these, the parts toward the east and toward the south might signify the two orders of those who have attained progress according to God. One order consists of those perfected in knowledge and word, and in the other gifts of the divine Spirit; the other consists of those who succeed through their way of life, and who persevere in blessings. The remaining two parts, divided from the former, would be those toward the sea and toward the north,

> "both signified as being toward wickedness. For from the north, he says, evils will be kindled upon all who dwell on the earth; and he says the dragon makes his dwelling upon the sea; so that reasonably here, too, two ways of those falling away from the Church are indicated, both those who sin in knowledge and those who sin in character, so that these are the divisions of the mount of Olives hinted at by the prophecy." Following these, it is added, "And the valley of my mountains shall be stopped up, and the valley of the mountains shall be joined as far as Asael; and it shall be stopped up just as it was stopped up from the face of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah the king."

<summary>Eusebius interprets the prophecy of the Mount of Olives splitting in Zechariah as a dual allegory: first, the global expansion of the Church in all directions, and second, the division of the Church into different spiritual states and the emergence of heresies.</summary>
<keywords>Mount of Olives, Church, Jerusalem, prophecy, Zechariah, schism, heresy, spiritual interpretation</keywords>

text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
in the Acts of the Apostles <note>original: "πράξεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων"</note> he teaches, saying: While they were looking on, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him from their sight. And as they were gazing into heaven while he went, behold, two men stood by them in white robes, who also said: Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven. To which he adds, saying: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is opposite Jerusalem.

Now, according to the literal wording, "opposite Jerusalem" refers to the mountain situated to its east, the Mount of Olives. However, according to the deeper meaning <note>original: "κατὰ τὴν διάνοιαν"</note>, it refers to the holy Church of Christ and the mountain upon which it is founded. Concerning this, the Savior teaches, saying: A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden. It has been raised up in place of the fallen Jerusalem which did not rise again, and it is trodden by the feet of the Lord. Not only is it opposite Jerusalem, but it is also to its east, having received the rays of the light of godliness. It has become far superior to Jerusalem, drawing near to the Sun of Righteousness itself, concerning whom it has been said: But for you who fear me, the Sun of Righteousness shall rise.

The next part says that the Mount of Olives shall be split, half of it toward the east and the sea, a very great chaos, and half of it shall tilt toward the north, and half of it toward the south. This can signify the expansion of the Church throughout the whole inhabited world, since the east and the eastern nations have been filled. It also extends to the western sea and the islands within it. Furthermore, it has reached the south and the midday regions, as well as the north and the arctic. For everywhere the valley of the aforementioned victorious Lord, which is his Church, has been planted.

According to the deeper meaning, it can also hint at the divisions and heresies that have occurred and are still occurring within the Church of Christ, as well as the moral lapses and falls in conduct. For it says the mountain, being split, shall be divided in two: half of it toward the east, half of it toward the sea, a very great chaos, and half of the mountain shall tilt toward the north, and half of it toward the south. Thus it is divided into four parts: two being more venerable and better, and two being the opposite. Consider whether through these the parts toward the east and the south signify two ranks of those who have attained progress according to God. One rank consists of those perfected in knowledge and word <note>original: "ἐν γνώσει καὶ λόγῳ"</note> and the other gifts of the Divine Spirit; the other consists of those who live uprightly through their conduct, persevering in blessings.

The remaining two parts, separated from the former, would be those toward the sea and the north, both signifying evil. For it says: From the north shall evils flare up against all the inhabitants of the earth; and it says the dragon makes his haunts upon the sea. So it is reasonable that here also two ways are shown for those who fall away from the Church: those who sin in respect to knowledge, and those who sin in respect to character. These are the divisions of the Mount of Olives hinted at by the prophecy. Following these things, it is added: And the valley of my mountains shall be blocked up, and the valley of the mountains shall be joined as far as Azal; and it shall be blocked up in the same way it was blocked up before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king <note>The text breaks off here at the end of the page.</note>

<summary>Eusebius interprets the prophecy of the Mount of Olives from Zechariah, linking the mountain's physical location to the spiritual rise of the Church and its global expansion, while also allegorizing its "splitting" as the division between the faithful and heretics.</summary>
<keywords>Mount of Olives, Jerusalem, Church of Christ, Acts of the Apostles, Zechariah, allegory, heresy, Sun of Righteousness, geography of faith</keywords>

> he teaches in the Acts of the Apostles, saying: "While they were looking on, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him away from their eyes. And as they were gazing into heaven while he went, behold, two men stood beside them in white garments, who also said: Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him going into heaven." To this he adds: "Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is opposite Jerusalem." Now,

according to the literal wording, "opposite Jerusalem" refers to the mountain to the east of the city, the one known as the Mount of Olives. According to the deeper sense, however, it is the holy Church of Christ, and the mountain

> on which she is founded, about which the Saviour teaches when he says, "A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden," that has been raised up in place of the Jerusalem that fell and did not rise again,

and is trodden by the feet of the Lord. She is not only opposite Jerusalem, but also to the east of it, having received the rays of the light of godliness, and having come to stand far ahead of Jerusalem, and drawing near to the very Sun of

> righteousness, of whom it is said: "But for those who fear me the sun of righteousness shall rise." As for what
> the next passage says, that "the Mount of Olives shall be split, half of it toward the east
> and the sea, a very great chasm, and half of it shall lean toward the north, and
> half of it toward the south," this may signify the spreading out of the Church over the whole inhabited world of mankind,

since she has filled even the rising of the sun and the very peoples of the dawn and the East. She stretches also to the western sea, and to the islands in it. Indeed she has reached the south and the noonday region as well, and the north and the Bear. For everywhere the whole valley of the Lord, foretold as a sign of his victory, that is, his Church, has been planted. But the passage may also, in its deeper sense, hint at the schisms and heresies that have arisen in the Church of Christ and are arising even now, and at the fallings away in morals and in conduct of life. For it says that the mountain, once split, shall be cut in two, half of it toward the east, half of it toward the sea, a very great chasm, and half of the mountain shall lean toward the north, and half of it toward the south. So it is divided into four parts: two that are the more honourable and the better, and two that are the opposite. And consider whether by these words the part toward the east and the part toward the south may signify two orders of those who have laid hold of progress in the things of God: one made up of those perfected in knowledge and in word and in the other gifts of the divine Spirit; the other, of those who achieve uprightness through their way of life, and who persevere in blessings. The remaining two parts, divided off from the former, would be the one toward the sea and the one toward the north,

> both of them marked out as tending toward wickedness. "For from the region of the north," it says, "evils
> shall be kindled upon all who dwell on the earth"; and the dragon is said to make his haunts in the
> sea. So it is fitting that here too, of those who

fall away from the Church, two kinds are again indicated: those who sin in the matter of knowledge and those who sin through their character. These, then, are the divisions of the Mount of Olives in question that the prophecy hints at. Next after these words it adds: "And the

> valley of my mountains shall be blocked up, and the ravine of the mountains shall be joined together as far as Asael; and it shall be
> blocked up as it was blocked up from the face of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king

<summary>Eusebius reads Zechariah's prophecy of the Mount of Olives as fulfilled in the Ascension recorded in Acts, and interprets the mountain spiritually as the Church of Christ raised up in place of fallen Jerusalem. The splitting of the mountain into four parts signifies either the Church's spread to the four quarters of the world or the division between two orders of the faithful and two kinds of those who fall away through heresy and immoral life.</summary>

reference.text:
INTRODUCTION
Two ways of considering our Saviour Jesus Christ have
been illustrated in the previous book of the Proof of the Gospel: the first takes us above nature and beyond it: on its road we defined Him to be the Only-begotten Son of
God, or the Word Who is of the essence of God, the secondary cause of the Universe, or a spiritual substance, and the firstborn nature of God all-perfect, His holy and perfect Power before things created, or the spiritual image of the Unbegotten nature. The second was akin and more familiar to ourselves; on its road we defined Christ as the Word of God, proclaiming in human nature the holiness of the Father, according as He appeared in human form long before to those with Abraham, that famous ruler of the men of God, and was predicted to
appear again among men by human birth, and with flesh like ours, and to suffer the extremest shame. This being so, the argument will proceed in its natural order, if I proceed to display the prophetic evidence about Him, if, that is to say, we make our chief aim to discover what was essential in the promises made, and justify the Divinity ascribed to Him in the Gospels from the ancient prophetic evidence. And it will be necessary
first to discuss the nature of prophetic inspiration among the Hebrews, from whom we learned beforehand what they proclaimed. Greeks and Barbarians alike testify to the existence of oracles and oracular responses in all parts of the earth, and they say that they were revealed by the foresight of the Creator for the use and profit of men, so that there need be no essential difference between Hebrew prophecy
and the oracles of the other nations. For as the Supreme God gave oracles to the Hebrews through their prophets, and suggested what was to their advantage, so also He gave them to the other nations through their local oracles. For He was not only the God of the Jews, but of the rest of mankind as well; and He cared not more for these than those, but His Providence was over all alike, just as He has given the sun ungrudgingly for all, and not for the Hebrews only, and the supply of needs according to the seasons, and a like bodily constitution for all, and one
mode of birth, and one kind of rational soul. And, thus, they say he provided ungrudgingly for all men the science of foretelling the future, to some by prophets, to some by oracles, to some by the flight of birds, or by inspecting entrails, or by dreams, or omens contained in word or sound, or by some other sign. For these they say were bestowed on all men by the Providence of God, so that the prophets of the Hebrews should not seem to have an advantage over the rest of the world.
This, then, is their contention. Mine will meet it in this manner. If any argument could prove that the gods, or divine powers, or good daemons
[context] really presided over the oracles named, or over the omens from birds, or any of those referred to, I should have to yield to what was stated, that the Supreme God had given these things as well as the Hebrew prophecy to those who used them, for their good.

### Introduction.

<note>A decorative woodcut initial 'Ε' features a seated figure, likely a scholar or saint, holding a book within an ornate floral and architectural frame.</note>

Since the discourse regarding our Savior, Jesus Christ, has already shone forth in the treatise on this subject, the <term>Evangelical Demonstration</term> <gloss>Eusebius's work, Demonstratio Evangelica</gloss>: first, the transcendent and supreme <note>original: "ὑπερφυὴς καὶ ἐπέκεινα"</note> nature, by which we define Him to be the only-begotten Son of God, or the essential Word of God, the second cause of all things, or an intellectual essence and the virtuous nature near to God, the divine and blessed power before created things, or the intellectual image of the unbegotten nature; and second, the nature related to us and more familiar, by which we again define Him as the Word of God within man, the herald of the Father's piety, by which He appeared long ago in the form of a man to those around Abraham; and since it was previously foretold that He who wishes to be clearly seen by those who love God will again appear to men through human nature and flesh similar to ours, and will suffer indignities: let the argument proceed by way and order through us for the One who is about to set forth the prophetic testimonies concerning Him, if it is profitable, and let us first examine the promises, and confirm the theology concerning Him in the Gospels through the ancient and prophetic testimony. It is necessary to first examine what the manner of inspiration was among the Hebrew prophets, from whom we were previously instructed in the things foretold.

->The manner by which the prophets among the Hebrews both predicted future events and illuminated the only true theology.<-

<margin>M</margin> Greeks and barbarians everywhere recall that oracles and shrines existed. They claim these were established by the providence of the Creator for the use and benefit of humanity, so that there is no difference between the prophets of the Hebrews and the oracles of other nations. Just as God over all spoke to the Hebrews through their own prophets, so too did He speak to other nations through their own oracles, suggesting what was profitable. For He is not the God of the Jews only, but of all other men as well. He cares no more for the former than for the latter, and He sends His providence equally, just as the sun is given abundantly to all, and not to the Hebrews alone. And so too are the yearly provisions of necessities, the similar construction of bodies for all, and the one way provided directly to all, and the one nature of the rational soul. Thus, the knowledge of the foreknowledge of future events is provided abundantly to all men—to some through prophetic men, to others through oracles, to others through the flight of birds, or through sacrifice, or through dream-sending, or through omens, or twitchings, or other signs. For they say these things were given to men by the providence of God, so that the prophets of the Hebrews might not seem to have any advantage. Such is the argument from them. But our own argument shall respond to them in this way: If any account establishes those who are truly gods, or divine powers, or demons...

EUSEBIUS

### Preface.

<note>A decorative woodcut initial 'E' depicts a seated figure, likely a scholar or saint, holding a book within an ornate floral and architectural frame.</note>

Since the discourse concerning our Savior Jesus Christ has already appeared in the work on the Evangelical Demonstration, it is necessary to proceed in order. We have defined Him in one sense as transcendent and beyond, as the only-begotten Son of God, or the essential Word of God, the second cause of all things, or an intellectual essence and a nature near to God, the divine and blessed power before all created things, or the intellectual image of the unbegotten nature. In another sense, we have defined Him as akin to us and more familiar, as the Word of God in man, the revealer of the Father's piety, as He appeared long ago in the form of a man to those around Abraham. Let it be foretold that He who wished to be clearly manifest to those who love God, and who would appear again among men through human nature and flesh similar to ours, would suffer things that cannot be described. As we prepare to set forth the prophetic testimonies concerning Him, if it is beneficial, let us first examine the promises and confirm the theology concerning Him in the Gospels through the ancient and prophetic testimony. It is necessary to first examine what the manner of divine inspiration was among the Hebrew prophets, from whom we have been instructed in the things foretold.

->The manner in which the Hebrew prophets both foretold future events and illuminated the only true theology.<-

<margin>M</margin>Greeks and barbarians everywhere speak of the existence of oracles and shrines. They claim these were established by the providence of the Creator for the use and benefit of mankind, such that there is no difference between the Hebrew prophets and the oracles of other nations. They argue that just as God, who is over all, gave oracles to the Hebrews through their own prophets, so too did He give them to other nations through their own shrines, providing them with what is beneficial. They claim that God is not the God of the Jews alone, but of all other men as well, and that He cares for them no less than for the Jews. They argue that He sends His providence equally to all, just as He has generously given the sun to everyone, and not only to the Hebrews. They point to the annual provision of necessities, the similar construction of bodies for all, and the one way and one nature of the rational soul given directly to all. In this way, they claim He provides the knowledge of foretelling the future to all men abundantly: to some through prophetic men, to others through shrines, to others through the flight of birds, or through sacrifice, or through dreams, or through omens, or through twitches, or other such symbols. They claim these were given to men by the providence of God, so that the Hebrew prophets appear to have no advantage. Such is their argument. Our response to them will be as follows: if any argument establishes that these are truly gods, or divine powers, or demons

<summary>Eusebius introduces the prophetic tradition of the Hebrews as the foundation for understanding the nature of Christ, while contrasting it with the pagan belief in oracles and divination as universal manifestations of divine providence.</summary>

<margin>Μ</margin>αντεῖα καὶ χρηστήρια πανταχόσε γῆς ἕλληνες καὶ βάρβαροι μνημονεύουσι συστῆναι. ταῦτα δὲ φασὶν ἐκ προνοίας τοῦ δημιουργοῦ ἐπὶ χρῆσιν καὶ ὠφέλειαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων καταδεδείχθαι, ὡς μηδὲν εἶναι τὸ διαφέρον τῶν παρ’ ἑβραίοις προφητῶν, πρὸς τὰ τῶν λοιπῶν ἐθνῶν χρηστήρια. ὡς γὰρ ἑβραίοις διὰ τῶν ἰδίων προφητῶν, οὕτω καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις ἔθνεσι διὰ τῶν παρ’ αὐτοῖς μαντείων τὸν ἐπὶ πάντων θεὸν χρᾶν, καὶ τὰ συμφέροντα ὑποτίθεσθαι. μὴ γὰρ ἰουδαίων μόνον εἶναι θεὸν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ἁπάντων ἀνθρώπων. καὶ οὐ μᾶλλον ἐκείνων, ἢ τούτων κήδεσθαι, πέμπειν δ’ ἐξ ἴσου προνοεῖν, ὡς ἀφροῦν τὸν ἥλιον ἀφθόνως τοῖς πᾶσι δεδωρῆσθαι, ἀλλ’ οὐ μόνοις ἑβραίοις. καὶ τὰς ἐτησίους τῶν ἐπιτηδείων χορηγίας, σωμάτων τε τοῖς πᾶσι κατασκευὴν ὁμοίαν, ἕνα τε ἀμέσως τοῖς πᾶσι τρόπον, καὶ φύσιν λογικῆς ψυχῆς μίαν. οὕτω δὲ καὶ τὴν τῶν μελλόντων προγνώσεως τὴν ἐπιστήμην πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ἀφθόνως παρέχειν, τοῖς μὲν διὰ προφητῶν ἀνδρῶν, τοῖς δὲ διὰ χρηστηρίων, τοῖς δὲ διὰ ὀρνίθων πτήσεως, ἢ διὰ θυτικῆς, ἢ δι’ ὀνειροπομπίας, ἢ διὰ κληδόνων, ἢ παλμῶν, ἢ τινων ἑτέρων συμβόλων. ταῦτα γάρ φασιν ἀνθρώποις ἐκ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ προνοίας δεδωρῆσθαι, ὡς μηδὲν πλέον ἔχειν δοκεῖν τοὺς ἑβραίων προφήτας. τοιοῦτος μὲν οὖν ὁ παρ’ ἐκείνων λόγος. ὁ δὲ παρ’ ἡμῶν, ὧδέ πως αὐτοῖς ἀπαντήσεται. εἰ μὲν τις συνίστη λόγος θεοῖς ἀληθῶς, ἢ θείας δυνάμεις, ἢ δαίμονας

### Introduction

<note>A decorative woodcut initial E featuring a seated figure, possibly a scholar or saint, holding a book within an ornate floral and architectural frame.</note>

Since the remaining discourse concerning our Savior Jesus Christ has been made clear in this treatise of the *Evangelical Proof* <note>original: "Euangelikes Apodeixeos"</note>; on the one hand, he is supernatural and beyond, according to which we define him to be the only-begotten Son of God, or the essential Word of God, the second cause of all things, or an intellectual essence and the virtuous nature closest to God, the divine and blessed power before created things, or the intellectual image of the unbegotten nature. On the other hand, he is related to us and more familiar, according to which we again define him as the Word of God in man, the one who furrows the field of the Father's piety, according to which he appeared long ago in human form to those around Abraham. Let it be said beforehand that this very one, wishing to appear clearly to those who love God, and being destined to appear again among men through a human nature and flesh similar to ours, would suffer things beyond anointing. Let the discourse proceed by way of order and sequence through us, as we intend to set forth the prophetic testimonies concerning him, if indeed they are beneficial; and let us first examine the promises and confirm the theologies concerning him in the Gospels from the ancient and prophetic testimony. It is necessary to first examine what was the manner of the divine inspiration <note>term: theolepsia</note> of the prophets among the Hebrews, from whom we have been previously instructed in the things foretold.

->What is the manner by which the prophets among the Hebrews both foretold the future and illuminated the only true theology?<-

<margin>M</margin> Oracles and shrines are remembered by Greeks and barbarians alike to have been established everywhere on earth. They say these were demonstrated by the providence of the Creator for the use and benefit of men, so that there is no difference between the prophets among the Hebrews and the shrines of the other nations. For just as God spoke to the Hebrews through their own prophets, so also he spoke to the other nations through the oracles among them, and suggested things that were beneficial. For they argue God is not the God of the Jews alone, but also of all other men. And he does not care for the former more than the latter, but sends his providence equally, just as the sun has been given ungrudgingly to all, and not to the Hebrews alone. So too the annual supplies of necessities, the similar construction of bodies for all, and in one way directly for all, a single nature of the rational soul. Thus also he provides the knowledge of the foreknowledge of future things ungrudgingly to all men, to some through prophetic men, to others through shrines, to others through the flight of birds, or through sacrificial divination, or through the sending of dreams, or through omens, or palpitations, or certain other symbols. For they say these things were given to men from the providence of God, so that the prophets of the Hebrews seem to have nothing more. Such then is the argument from them. But the argument from us will meet them in this way. If indeed any argument established that they were truly gods, or divine powers, or spirits <note>term: daimones</note>...

<summary>Eusebius introduces the second part of his work, defining the nature of Christ and beginning an investigation into how Hebrew prophecy differs from pagan oracles and divination.</summary>

[context] For if our most Divine Altar is Jesus--the supremely Divine sanctifying of the Godly Minds --in Whom, according to the Logion, "being sanctified and mystically offered as a whole burnt-offering, we have the access," let us gaze with supermundane eyes upon the most Divine Altar itself (in which things being perfected, are perfected and sanctified), being perfected from the most Divine Muron itself; for the altogether most holy Jesus sanctifies Himself on our behalf, and fills us full of every sanctification,
since the things consecrated upon them pass fraternally afterwards in their beneficent effects to us, as children of God. Hence, as I think, the Divine Leaders of our Hierarchy, in conformity with a Hierarchical conception divinely transmitted, name this altogether august ministration "consecration of Muron," from "being consecrated thoroughly," as one might say, "consecration of God," extolling its divine consecrating work in each sense. For both the being sanctified for our sakes, as becomes Man, and the consecrating all things as supreme God, and the sanctifying things being consecrated, is "consecration of Him." As for the sacred song of the inspiration of the God-rapt Prophets, it is called by those who know Hebrew, the "Praise of God," or "Praise ye the Lord," for since every divine manifestation and work of God is reverently portrayed in the varied composition of the Hierarchical symbols, it is not unfitting to mention the Divinely moved song of the Prophets; for it teaches at once, distinctly and reverently, that the beneficent works of the Divine Goodness are worthy of devout praise.

text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
while the things done in it through the divine plan flow down to us beneficially, as to those born of God. Therefore, in my opinion, according to the hierarchical sense handed down by God, the divine leaders of our sacred order call this most venerable and holy mystery of the <term>Ointment</term> <gloss>original Greek: Myron</gloss> a <term>telete</term> <gloss>consecration or perfecting rite</gloss>, because it actually consecrates and perfects. It is as if one spoke of the "consecration of God," praising his divine perfection in both senses. For it is the consecration of God, both because he is sanctified in a human way for our sake, and because he himself, in a divine way, consecrates and sanctifies everything that is to be consecrated. Furthermore, those who know Hebrew say that the sacred melody of the divinely inspired prophets signifies the praise of God, or "Praise the Lord" <note>original: "Laudate Dominum", referring to the word Alleluia</note>. Since, therefore, every sacred appearance of God and every divine operation is described in the varied composition of hierarchical symbols, it is by no means out of place to remember the praise of the prophets which they learned from God. For it teaches clearly and holily that the divine benefits are worthy of the highest praise.

<column-break/>

<margin>Text of ST. DIONYSIUS</margin>

...while the things done in them through the divine plan flow down to us beneficially, as to those born of God. From this, I believe, according to the hierarchical mind and divine tradition, the divine leaders of our hierarchy call this most venerable ceremony the <term>consecration of the Ointment</term> <gloss>original Greek: Myrou teleten</gloss>, naming it from the actual perfecting it performs. It is as if one said "the consecration of God," praising its divine perfecting power in both meanings. For it is his consecration, both in his being sanctified in a human manner for us, and in his divine performing and sanctifying of all things that are consecrated. Those who know the language of the Hebrews say that the sacred melody of the divinely inspired prophets signifies the praise of God, or "Praise the Lord." Since every sacred manifestation of God and divine operation is inscribed in the varied arrangement of hierarchical symbols, it is not unfitting to mention the divinely-moved song of the prophets. It teaches, in a way both pure and fitting for sacred things, that the divine acts of goodness are worthy of sacred praise.

dum ea quae in eo geruntur per dispensationem, ad nos, veluti à Deo genitos, beneficè dimanant. Vnde, ut opinor, iuxta sensum Hierarchicum qui à Deo traditus est, diuini isti sacri nostri ordinis duces sanctum hoc Vnguenti myste-
<margin>

rium *teleten*, id est consecrationem vocant, quòd re ipsa consecret atque consummet; ut si quis dixerit Dei consecrationem, utroque sensu diuinam eius perfectionem praedicando. Est enim Dei consecratio, cùm quòd propter nos humanitus sanctificetur, tum quòd diuinitus cuncta, quae consecranda sunt, ipse consecret atque sanctificet. Porrò melos illud sacrum Prophetarum diuinitus afflatorum, aiunt hi qui Hebraicè norunt, Dei laudem significare, siue *Laudate Dominum*. Cùm igitur sacra omnis Dei apparitio actione in diuersa Hierarchicorum symbolorum compositione sit descripta, nequaquam abs re fuerit, meminisse laudationis Prophetarum quam diuinitus didicerunt: docet enim praeclarè simul ac sanctè, diuina beneficia praecipua laude digna esse.

τῶν ἐπ’ αὐτῶν τελουμένων οἰκονομικῶς εἰς ἡμᾶς, ὡς θεογεννήτοις, λοιπὸν ἀγαθουργικῶς διαβαινόντων. Ὅθεν, ὡς οἶμαι, κατὰ νοῦν ἱεραρχικὸν θεοπαραδότως οἱ θεῖοι τῆς καθ’ ἡμᾶς ἱεραρχίας καθηγεμόνες, τὴν πάνσεμνον καὶ ταύτην ἱερουργίαν Μύρου τελετήν, ἐκ τῆς τελουμένου πραγματικῶς ὀνομάζουσιν; ὡς ἄν τις φαίη Θεοῦ τελετήν, ἑκατέρῳ νῷ τὴν θείαν αὐτῆς τελετουργίαν ὑμνοῦντες. Ἔστι γὰρ αὐτοῦ τελετή, καὶ τὸ δι’ ἡμᾶς ἀνθρωποπρεπῶς ἁγιάζεσθαι, καὶ τὸ θεουργικῶς ἅπαντα τελεῖν καὶ ἁγιάζειν τὰ τελούμενα. Τὸ δὲ ἱερὸν τῆς τῶν θεολήπτων Προφητῶν ἐπιπνοίας μελώδημα, φασὶν οἱ τὰ Ἑβραίων εἰδότες, τὸ αἶνον Θεοῦ δηλοῦν, ἢ τὸ Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον. Ἁπάσης οὖν ἱερᾶς θεοφανείας καὶ θεουργίας ἐν τῇ ποικίλῃ συνθέσει τῶν ἱεραρχικῶν συμβόλων ἱερογραφουμένης, οὐκ ἀνάρμοστόν ἐστι μεμνῆσθαι τῆς θεοκινήτου τῶν Προφητῶν ὑμνολογίας· διδάσκει γὰρ εὐαγῶς τε ἅμα καὶ ἱεροπρεπῶς, αἴνων ἱερῶν ἀξίας εἶναι τὰς θεαρχικὰς ἀγαθουργίας.

reasons.j1: Both columns are rendered and agree with the source: Latin 'quòd re ipsa consecret atque consummet' = 'because it actually consecrates and perfects'; Greek 'ἑκατέρῳ νῷ ... ὑμνοῦντες' = 'praising ... in both meanings', 'αἴνων ἱερῶν ἀξίας ... τὰς θεαρχικὰς ἀγαθουργίας' = 'divine acts of goodness are worthy of sacred praise', matching the reference's sense. Nothing wrong found; only the side-note 'Vnguentum quare τελετὴ dictum' and 'λοιπὸν' are unrendered, and the Alleluia note is correct. Reference covers the Greek column only.
reasons.j2: Both columns rendered: the Latin ('teleten, id est consecrationem vocant, quòd re ipsa consecret atque consummet') and the Greek ('Μύρου τελετήν … Θεοῦ τελετήν, ἑκατέρῳ νῷ') agree with the source and with the reference for the Greek; only a marginal caption and 'λοιπὸν' are missing. Reference covers the Greek column only.

served.note: Plain modern prose, easy to follow; keeps telete and glosses it with both senses, flags the Alleluia identification in a note; the hieratic Dionysian voice is thinned; renders both the Latin and Greek columns.

reference.note: Dense, capitalised, hieratic diction that matches the Areopagite's voice but is hard going; keeps Muron, renders telete uniformly as consecration so the perfect/consecrate play is only half visible; no flags.

six_dimensions.choice: A keeps the rite's name as a glossed term ("a <term>telete</term> <gloss>consecration or perfecting rite</gloss>") while B translates it and keeps the unguent's name ("consecration of Muron").

text:
S. DIONYSII AREOPAGITÆ

<margin>Text of S. DIONYSIUS.</margin>
while those things which are performed within it through dispensation flow down to us, as if to those born of God, in a beneficent manner. Whence, as I suppose, according to the Hierarchical sense which has been handed down by God, those divine leaders of our sacred order call this holy mystery of the Ointment a <term>teleten</term> <gloss>consecration</gloss>, because it truly consecrates and perfects; just as if one were to speak of the consecration of God, praising His divine perfection in both senses. For it is the consecration of God, both because He is sanctified in a human manner for our sake, and because He Himself divinely consecrates and sanctifies all things that are to be consecrated. Furthermore, those who know Hebrew say that that sacred melody of the divinely inspired Prophets signifies the praise of God, or "Praise the Lord." Since, therefore, every sacred manifestation of God is described by action in the diverse composition of Hierarchical symbols, it would by no means be out of place to remember the praise of the Prophets which they learned from God; for it teaches clearly and holily that divine benefits are worthy of supreme praise.

<margin>Why the Ointment is called a <term>teleten</term> <gloss>consecration</gloss>.</margin>

<column-break/>

of those things performed upon them economically, as if to those born of God, subsequently passing over in a beneficent manner. Whence, as I suppose, according to the Hierarchical mind handed down by God, the divine leaders of our hierarchy call this most holy sacred rite the Consecration of the Myrrh, from the fact that it is truly performed; as one might say the Consecration of God, praising its divine perfection in both senses. For it is His consecration, both the being sanctified in a human manner for our sake, and the divinely perfecting and sanctifying of all things that are being consecrated. And the sacred melody of the divinely inspired Prophets, those who know the Hebrew language say, signifies the praise of God, or "Praise the Lord." Since, therefore, every sacred manifestation of God and divine action is written in the diverse composition of Hierarchical symbols, it is not inappropriate to remember the God-moved hymnody of the Prophets; for it teaches piously and at the same time in a manner befitting the sacred, that the divine benefactions are worthy of sacred praises.

<summary>This page discusses the theological significance of the "Consecration of the Myrrh" within the Dionysian hierarchy, explaining how the term "teleten" (consecration) reflects both the human sanctification of God and the divine sanctification of all things.</summary>
<keywords>Dionysius the Areopagite, Consecration of the Myrrh, teleten, hierarchy, divine benefaction, hymnody, Prophets</keywords>

<margin>

</margin>
dum ea quae in eo geruntur per dispensationem, ad nos, veluti à Deo genitos, beneficè dimanant. Vnde, ut opinor, iuxta sensum Hierarchicum qui à Deo traditus est, diuini isti sacri nostri ordinis duces sanctum hoc Vnguenti myste-
<margin>
Vnguentum quare τελετὴ dictum.
</margin>
rium *teleten*, id est consecrationem vocant, quòd re ipsa consecret atque consummet; ut si quis dixerit Dei consecrationem, utroque sensu diuinam eius perfectionem praedicando. Est enim Dei consecratio, cùm quòd propter nos humanitus sanctificetur, tum quòd diuinitus cuncta, quae consecranda sunt, ipse consecret atque sanctificet. Porrò melos illud sacrum Prophetarum diuinitus afflatorum, aiunt hi qui Hebraicè norunt, Dei laudem significare, siue *Laudate Dominum*. Cùm igitur sacra omnis Dei apparitio actione in diuersa Hierarchicorum symbolorum compositione sit descripta, nequaquam abs re fuerit, meminisse laudationis Prophetarum quam diuinitus didicerunt: docet enim praeclarè simul ac sanctè, diuina beneficia praecipua laude digna esse.

<column-break/>

<language>Ancient Greek</language>
τῶν ἐπ’ αὐτῶν τελουμένων οἰκονομικῶς εἰς ἡμᾶς, ὡς θεογεννήτοις, λοιπὸν ἀγαθουργικῶς διαβαινόντων. Ὅθεν, ὡς οἶμαι, κατὰ νοῦν ἱεραρχικὸν θεοπαραδότως οἱ θεῖοι τῆς καθ’ ἡμᾶς ἱεραρχίας καθηγεμόνες, τὴν πάνσεμνον καὶ ταύτην ἱερουργίαν Μύρου τελετήν, ἐκ τῆς τελουμένου πραγματικῶς ὀνομάζουσιν; ὡς ἄν τις φαίη Θεοῦ τελετήν, ἑκατέρῳ νῷ τὴν θείαν αὐτῆς τελετουργίαν ὑμνοῦντες. Ἔστι γὰρ αὐτοῦ τελετή, καὶ τὸ δι’ ἡμᾶς ἀνθρωποπρεπῶς ἁγιάζεσθαι, καὶ τὸ θεουργικῶς ἅπαντα τελεῖν καὶ ἁγιάζειν τὰ τελούμενα. Τὸ δὲ ἱερὸν τῆς τῶν θεολήπτων Προφητῶν ἐπιπνοίας μελώδημα, φασὶν οἱ τὰ Ἑβραίων εἰδότες, τὸ αἶνον Θεοῦ δηλοῦν, ἢ τὸ Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον. Ἁπάσης οὖν ἱερᾶς θεοφανείας καὶ θεουργίας ἐν τῇ ποικίλῃ συνθέσει τῶν ἱεραρχικῶν συμβόλων ἱερογραφουμένης, οὐκ ἀνάρμοστόν ἐστι μεμνῆσθαι τῆς θεοκινήτου τῶν Προφητῶν ὑμνολογίας· διδάσκει γὰρ εὐαγῶς τε ἅμα καὶ ἱεροπρεπῶς, αἴνων ἱερῶν ἀξίας εἶναι τὰς θεαρχικὰς ἀγαθουργίας.

while those things which are performed in it through the divine dispensation flow down to us, as those born of God, in a manner of doing good. Hence, as I believe, according to the <term>Hierarchical</term> <gloss>sacred order</gloss> sense delivered by God, those divine leaders of our sacred order call this most venerable mystery of the <term>Ointment</term> <gloss>Myron or holy oil</gloss> a <term>teleten</term> <gloss>consecration or perfecting rite</gloss>, because it actually consecrates and completes. It is as if one were to say "the consecration of God," praising His divine perfection in both senses. For it is the consecration of God, both because He is sanctified in a human way for our sake, and because He Himself, in a divine way, consecrates and sanctifies all things that are to be consecrated. Furthermore, that sacred melody of the divinely inspired Prophets, as those who know Hebrew say, signifies the praise of God, or <term>Alleluia</term> <gloss>Praise the Lord</gloss>. Since, therefore, every sacred appearance of God is described in action through the diverse composition of hierarchical symbols, it would by no means be out of place to remember the praise of the Prophets which they learned from God; for it teaches clearly and holily that the divine benefits are worthy of the highest praise.

<column-break/>

<meta>The following is the original Greek text of the passage translated above.</meta>

while those things performed in them through the divine dispensation pass over to us, as those born of God, in a manner of doing good. Hence, as I think, according to the hierarchical mind delivered by God, the divine leaders of our hierarchy call this most venerable sacred rite the <term>Myrou teleten</term> <gloss>consecration of the Ointment</gloss>, naming it from the thing actually performed; as if one were to say "the consecration of God," praising its divine perfecting power in both senses of the mind. For it is His consecration, both in His being sanctified in a human manner for us, and in His divinely performing and sanctifying all things that are consecrated. And the sacred melody of the inspiration of the God-possessed Prophets, those who know the language of the Hebrews say, signifies the praise of God, or "Praise the Lord." Since every sacred manifestation of God and divine work is recorded in the varied composition of the hierarchical symbols, it is not unfitting to remember the God-moved hymnology of the Prophets; for it teaches purely and in a manner becoming to sacred things that the divine works of the <term>Thearchy</term> <gloss>divine rule or Godhead</gloss> are worthy of sacred praises.

<summary>Dionysius explains the naming of the Holy Ointment as a consecration or perfecting rite, linking it to both Christ's sanctification and the sanctification of the faithful. He also connects the liturgical use of the Ointment to the prophetic tradition of praising God.</summary>
<keywords>Myron, Ointment, Consecration, Telete, Hierarchy, Prophets, Praise, Sanctification, Divine Dispensation</keywords>

reference.text:
[context] Since we have arranged the many loves from the one, by telling, in due order, what are the kinds of
knowledge and powers of the mundane and supermundane loves; over which, according to the defined purpose of the discourse, the orders and ranks of the mental and intelligible loves preside; next after
which are placed the self-existent intelligible and divine, over the really beautiful loves there which have been appropriately celebrated by us; now, on the other hand, by restoring all back to the One and enfolded Love, and Father of them all, let us collect and gather them together from the many, by contracting It into two Powers entirely lovable, over which rules and precedes altogether the Cause, resistless from Its universal Love beyond all, and to which is elevated, according to the nature of each severally, the whole love from all existing things.
Of the same, from the same Hymns of Love.
Come then, whilst collecting these again into one, let us say, that it is a certain simplex power, which of itself moves to a sort of unifying combination from the Good, to the lowest of things existing, and from that again in due order, circling round again, through all to the Good from Itself, and through Itself and by Itself, and rolling back to Itself always in the same way.
And yet, any one might say, "if the Beautiful and Good is beloved and desired, and esteemed by all (for even that which is non-existing desires It, as we have said, and struggles how to be in It; and Itself is the form-giving, even of things without form, and by It alone, even the non-existing is said to be, and is superessentially)--"How is it that the host of demons do not desire the Beautiful and Good, but, through their earthly proclivities, having fallen away from the angelic identity, as regards the desire of the Good, have become cause of all evils both to themselves and to all the others who are said to be corrupted? and why, in short, when the tribes of demons have been brought into being from the Good, are they not like the Good? or how, after being a good production from the Good, were they changed?
and what is that which depraved them,
[context] and in short, what is evil? and from what source did it spring? and in which of things existing is it? and how did He, Who is Good, will to bring it into being? and how, when He willed it, was He able? And if evil is from another cause, what other cause is there for things existing, beside the Good? Further, how, when there is a Providence, is there evil, either coming into existence at all, or not destroyed? And how does any existing thing desire it, in comparison with the Good?

<meta>The text contains excerpts from the works of Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, specifically discussing the nature of the ecclesiastical and celestial hierarchies. The OCR for the second half of the page shows significant repetition of the word hierarchical, likely due to ink bleeding or script ligatures in the 10th-century manuscript.</meta>

gnostic <note>knowledge-bringing</note> and godlike wisdom, at least as much as is revealed to those initiated into it. For the hierarchical arrangements, celebrated in holy manifestations, are his method and the provision of beautiful things, through which the Supreme Good is formed within us. And to us, the stewards of the hierarchy reveal these sacred splendors, so that we might not be uninitiated in the things seen. And of these same sacred things, as many as are holy, we are not merely initiated. We are also more radiant than other men, because those who are first are shaped without artifice. Hence, this same [wisdom] is pure, and holy, and revealing of the sacred and mystical manifestations; it is hierarchical and it exercises hierarchy, revealing and being naturally joined to the things seen, while seeing the unseen without sight, because the divine man...

<margin>
The hierarchical and godlike nature of the hierarchy is a revelation of the sacred and mystical manifestations.
</margin>

### From the same author, from the writings On the Celestial Hierarchy.

This also is clear: that the things called sacred, and ancient, and hierarchical, are themselves also revealing, and hierarchical, and exercising hierarchy, and subject to hierarchy. And those initiated, as many as are sacred, and parts of these being hierarchical and revealed, as it were, the substantial things and the good, as hierarchical. And because of this, and hierarchical, hierarchical, as hierarchical, and exercising hierarchy. And as many of the sacred things, these are not the only ones. And to the gods, to us, made known from words and sacred vision, and seeing, and hierarchical. To see, hierarchical, and some of which he himself is hierarchical, and hierarchical, making them also hierarchical, and the hierarchical, and exercising hierarchy. And these, hierarchical of others, and hierarchical, and some of which are exercising hierarchy, hierarchical, hierarchical, making them hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, of the Lord and the True One. Similar, because sacred, and the things are hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, such as these, of this, hierarchical, hierarchical, and hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, and of himself, and the hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, and hierarchical, hierarchical, confessedly, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical.

<margin>
A hierarchical prayer.
</margin>

<summary>This page discusses how the divine hierarchy reveals sacred wisdom and mystical manifestations to the initiated. It emphasizes the role of hierarchy in shaping the soul toward the Supreme Good and mentions the Celestial Hierarchy.</summary>
<keywords>Pseudo-Dionysius, hierarchy, celestial hierarchy, mysticism, initiation, divine wisdom, revelation</keywords>

The first paragraph is only loosely coherent, and the second paragraph degenerates into disconnected words and long repetitions of a single word ("hierarchical"), which almost certainly do not reflect the manuscript. The translation below follows the transcription as given, word for word where no syntax can be recovered, and should not be cited as the text of Pseudo-Dionysius.</warning>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>

knowing and godlike wisdom, at least as much of it as is revealed to those who have been initiated into it. For the hierarchical and <unclear>μελισσόμεναι</unclear> orderings of the holy manifestations are a path to it and to its fair bestowals, and from them that which is beyond goodness takes form for us. And for us the stewards of the hierarchy unveil these sacred splendours, so that we may not be uninitiated in the things that are seen. And of the same sacred things, as many as are sacred, and not simply initiated. And more radiant than other men, because they themselves are the first and are set in order without pretence. Hence also the same, pure, and holy, and revelatory of the sacred and mystical manifestations, and hierarchical, and ruling as hierarch, revealing, being by nature akin to the things that are seen, being without sight the things unseen, because the divine man...

<margin>The hierarchical and godlike character of the hierarchy, revelatory of the sacred and mystical manifestations</margin>

By the same author, from the writings On the Celestial Hierarchy.

This too is clear, that the things called sacred, and ancient, and hierarchical, that these too are revelatory, and hierarchical, and ruling as hierarchs, and ruled by hierarchs, and the things initiated, as many as are sacred, and parts, and these being so, hierarchical, and revealed, as it might be, the things that give subsistence, and good, as hierarchical, and for this reason, also hierarchical, hierarchical, as hierarchical, and ruling as hierarchs. And as many of the sacred things, these, are not the only ones. And to the gods, to us, known, from words, and sacred things, sight, and seeing, and hierarchical. To see, hierarchical, and those of which, he himself, hierarchical, and hierarchical, making, and these themselves, hierarchical, and the hierarchical things, and ruling as hierarchs. And these, hierarchical, of others, and hierarchical, and those of which, ruling as hierarchs, hierarchical, hierarchical, making, and hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, of the Lord, and true. Resembling, that sacred, and the, is, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, such, of this, hierarchical, hierarchical, and hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, and of himself, and the, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, and hierarchical, hierarchical, by way of confession, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical, hierarchical.

<margin>Hierarchical prayer</margin>

<summary>The page speaks of a godlike wisdom revealed to the initiated and of the stewards of the hierarchy who unveil sacred splendours, then opens an excerpt headed as taken from On the Celestial Hierarchy. And it shall come to pass that the child which she shall bear, shall be
named by the name of the deceased, and his name shall not be blotted out of Israel.
And if the man should not be willing to take his brother's wife, then shall the woman go up to the gate to the elders, and she shall say, My husband's brother will not raise up the name of his brother in Israel, my husband's brother
has refused.
And the elders of his city shall call him, and speak to him; and if he stand and say, I will not take her:
then his brother's wife shall come forward before the elders, and shall loose one shoe from off his foot, and shall spit in his face, and shall answer and say, Thus shall they do to the man who will not build his brother's house in Israel.
And his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that has had his shoe loosed.
And if men should strive together, a man with his brother, and the wife of one of them should advance to rescue her husband out of the hand of him that smites him, and she should stretch forth her hand, and take hold of his private parts;
thou shalt cut off her hand; thine eye shall not spare her.
Thou shalt not have in thy bag divers weights, a great
and a small.
Thou shalt not have in thine house divers measures, a great
and a small.
Thou shalt have a true and just weight, and a true and just measure, that thou mayest live long upon the land which the Lord thy God gives thee for an inheritance.
For every one that does this is an abomination to the Lord thy God, even every one that does injustice.
Remember what things Amalec did to thee by the way, when thou wentest forth out of the land of Egypt:
how he withstood thee in the way, and harassed thy rear, even those that were weary behind thee, and thou didst hunger and wast weary; and he did not fear God.
And it shall come to pass whenever the Lord thy God shall have given thee rest from all thine enemies round about thee, in the land which the Lord thy God gives thee to inherit, thou shalt blot out the name of Amalec from under heaven, and shalt not forget to do it.
And it shall be when thou shalt have entered into the land, which the Lord thy God gives thee to inherit it, and thou shalt have inherited it, and thou shalt have dwelt upon it,
that thou shalt take of the first of the fruits of thy land, which the Lord thy God gives thee, and thou shalt put them into a basket, and thou shalt go to the place which the Lord thy God shall choose to have his name called there.
And thou shalt come to the priest who shall be in those days, and thou shalt say to him, I testify this day to the Lord my God, that I am come into the land which the Lord sware to our fathers to give to us.

10. and his name shall be called in Israel: "The house of him whose sandal was loosened."
11. If men are fighting together, a man with his brother, and the wife of one of them approaches to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and stretching out her hand she seizes his private parts,
12. you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not spare her.
13. There shall not be in your pouch a weight and a weight, a large one or a small one.
14. There shall not be in your house a measure and a measure, a large one or a small one;
15. a true and righteous weight shall be yours, and a true and righteous measure shall be yours, so that you may live long upon the land which the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance;
16. for everyone who does these things, everyone who does unrighteousness, is an abomination to the Lord your God.
17. Remember what <term>Amalek</term> <gloss>an ancient enemy of Israel</gloss> did to you on the way, when you were coming out of the land of <term>Aigyptos</term> <gloss>Egypt</gloss>,
18. how he stood against you on the way, and cut off your rear guard, those who were weary behind you, and you were hungry and tired, and he did not fear God.
19. And it shall be, when the Lord your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land which the Lord your God gives you to inherit, you shall blot out the name of <term>Amalek</term> from under heaven, and you shall not forget.

### CHAPTER 26.

1. And it shall be, when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you to inherit, and you take possession of it, and dwell in it,
2. that you shall take from the first fruits of the fruits of your land which the Lord your God gives you, and you shall put them into a basket, and go to the place which the Lord your God chooses for His name to be called there.
3. And you shall come to the priest who shall be in those days, and say to him: "I declare today to the Lord my God that I have entered into the land which the Lord swore to our fathers to give us."

<column-break/>

6. And it shall be that the infant who is born shall be established from the name of the deceased, and his name shall not be deleted from Israel.
7. But if the man is unwilling to take the wife of his brother, and the woman shall go up to the gate to the senate <note>original: "senatum"</note>, and shall say: "My husband's brother does not wish to raise up the name of his brother in Israel; my husband's brother has refused."
8. And the elders of his city shall call him, and they shall say to him, and he, standing, shall say: "I do not wish to take her."
9. And the wife of his brother, approaching before the elders, shall loosen one of his shoes from his foot, and shall spit in his face, and answering she shall say: "Thus they shall do to the man who will not build the house of his brother in Israel,"
10. and his name shall be called in Israel: "The house of the unshod."
11. If men are fighting together, a man with his brother, and the wife of one of them approaches to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and extending her hand she seizes his testicles,
12. you shall cut off her hand: your eye shall not spare her.
13. There shall not be in your bag a weight and a weight, large or small.
14. There shall not be in your house a measure and a measure, large or small.
15. A true and just weight shall be for you, and a true and just measure shall be for you, so that you may be long-lived upon the land which the Lord your God gives you by lot:
16. for every one who does these things, every one who does injustice, is an abomination to the Lord your God.
17. Remember whatever <term>Amalec</term> <gloss>Amalek</gloss> did to you on the way, when you were leaving the land of <term>Aegyptus</term> <gloss>Egypt</gloss>,
18. how he resisted you on the way, and struck the tail of your column, the weary ones behind you, and you were hungry and laboring, and he did not fear God.
19. And it shall be, after the Lord your God has made you rest from all your enemies who are around you in the land which the Lord your God gives you to inherit, you shall delete the name of <term>Amalec</term> from under heaven, and you shall not forget.

### CHAPTER 26.

1. And it shall be, if you have entered into the land which the Lord your God gives you to inherit, and you have inherited it, and have dwelt in it,
2. and you take from the first-fruits of the fruits of the land which the Lord your God gives you, and you put them in a basket, and you go to the place which the Lord your God has chosen for His name to be invoked there.
3. And you shall come to the priest who shall be in those days, and you shall say to him: "I announce today to the Lord my God, that I have entered into the land which the Lord swore to our fathers to give to us."

7. Ἐὰν δὲ μὴ βούληται ὁ ἄνθρωπος λαβεῖν τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναβήσεται ἡ γυνὴ ἐπὶ τὴν πύλην ἐπὶ τὴν γερουσίαν, καὶ ἐρεῖ· Οὐ θέλει ὁ ἀδελφὸς τοῦ ἀνδρός μου ἀναστῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ ἐν Ἰσραήλ, οὐκ ἠθέλησεν ὁ ἀδελφὸς τοῦ ἀνδρός μου.

9. καὶ προσελθοῦσα ἡ γυνὴ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ ἔναντι τῆς γερουσίας, καὶ ὑπολύσει τὸ ὑπόδημα αὐτοῦ τὸ ἓν ἀπὸ τοῦ ποδὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐμπτύσεται κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀποκριθεῖσα ἐρεῖ· Οὕτω ποιήσουσι τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ὃς οὐκ οἰκοδομήσει τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ ἐν Ἰσραήλ,
10. καὶ κληθήσεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐν Ἰσραήλ, οἶκος τοῦ ὑπολυθέντος τὸ ὑπόδημα.
11. Ἐὰν δὲ μάχωνται ἄνθρωποι ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ, ἄνθρωπος μετὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσέλθῃ ἡ γυνὴ ἑνὸς αὐτῶν ἐξελέσθαι τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς ἐκ χειρὸς τοῦ τύπτοντος αὐτὸν, καὶ ἐκτείνασα τὴν χεῖρα ἐπιλάβηται τῶν διδύμων αὐτοῦ,
12. ἀποκόψεις τὴν χεῖρα· οὐ φείσεται ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἐπ’ αὐτῇ.
13. Οὐκ ἔσται ἐν τῷ μαρσίππῳ σου στάθμιον καὶ στάθμιον, μέγα ἢ μικρόν.
14. Οὐκ ἔσται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ σου μέτρον καὶ μέτρον, μέγα ἢ μικρόν·
15. στάθμιον ἀληθινὸν καὶ δίκαιον ἔσται σοι, καὶ μέτρον ἀληθινὸν καὶ δίκαιον ἔσται σοι, ἵνα πολυήμερος γένῃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἧς Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου δίδωσί σοι ἐν κλήρῳ·
16. ὅτι βδέλυγμα Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ σου πᾶς ποιῶν ταῦτα, πᾶς ποιῶν ἄδικον.
17. Μνήσθητι ὅσα ἐποίησέ σοι Ἀμαλὴκ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ἐκπορευομένου σου ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου,
18. πῶς ἀντέστη σοι ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, καὶ ἔκοψέ σου τὴν οὐραγίαν τοὺς κοπιῶντας ὀπίσω σου, σὺ δὲ ἐπείνας καὶ ἐκοπίας, καὶ οὐκ ἐφοβήθη τὸν Θεόν.

2. καὶ λήψῃ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀπαρχῆς τῶν καρπῶν τῆς γῆς σου ἧς Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου δίδωσί σοι, καὶ ἐμβαλεῖς εἰς κάρταλλον, καὶ πορεύσῃ εἰς τὸν τόπον ὃν ἂν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου ἐπικληθῆναι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖ.

6. Et erit infans quicumque natus fuerit, constituetur ex defuncti nomine, et non delebitur nomen ejus ex Israel.

11. Si autem rixati fuerint homines pariter, homo cum fratre suo , et accesserit uxor unius eorum ad eruendum virum suum de manu verberantis eum, et extendens manum apprehenderit testes ejus,
12. abscindes manum : non parcet oculus tuus super eam.
13. Non erit in marsupio tuo pondus et pondus , magnum aut parvum.

15. Pondus verax et justum erit tibi , et mensura verax et justa erit tibi , ut longævus sis super terram quam Dominus Deus tuus dat tibi in sorte :
16. quoniam abominatio Domino Deo tuo omnis faciens hæc , omnis faciens injustum.

19. Et erit , postquam quiescere fecerit te Dominus Deus tuus ab omnibus inimicis tuis qui in circuitu tuo in terra quam Dominus Deus tuus dat tibi hæreditare, delebis nomen Amalec de sub cœlo , et non obliviscaris.

1. Et erit , si intraveris in terram quam Dominus tuus dat tibi hæreditare, et hæreditaveris eam, et habitaveris in ea,

3. Et venies ad sacerdotem qui erit in diebus illis , et dices ad eum : Annuntio hodie Domino Deo meo , quia intravi in terram quam juravit Dominus patribus nostris dare nobis.
